Subject: Ver, an elderly former dock worker waiting in a border settlement registration room. He is a slender man in his early seventies with a long weathered face, light warm skin, deep-set hazel eyes, swept-back fine silver hair with a receding hairline, and a clean-shaven chin. His expression is attentive and quietly resolute, with a gentle warmth around the eyes. He wears a faded burgundy-brown wool coat over a buff linen shirt and a loosely folded soft gray neckcloth. His posture is slightly stooped but dignified, his shoulders narrow, both empty hands held comfortably near the waist with relaxed fingers. His long silver hair and burgundy coat create a clear distinct silhouette. He conveys a person who wants his own name to be heard and preserved.
